# Genre

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:Genre`](gmeow-Genre.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/Genre>
- **Category:** class
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/creative-works`](../../slices/creative-works.md)
- **Box roles:** [TBox role](../boxes/tbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

A contested, registry-independent, lineage-bearing information object used to characterise creative works. Like [`gmeow:Language`](gmeow-Language.md), a genre is a first-class individual-bearing class; it is never a subclass tree and never a privileged winner of a genre dispute (Principles 5, 9).

## Structure

**Subclass of:** [`gmeow:InformationObject`](gmeow-InformationObject.md)

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:Genre`](gmeow-Genre.md) as a specialized kind of [`gmeow:InformationObject`](gmeow-InformationObject.md). Add statement metadata or a standpoint when the assertion needs provenance, confidence, or vantage.

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use to mint a genre as a first-class, contestable, lineage-bearing object that creative works point at via [`gmeow:hasGenre`](../properties/gmeow-hasGenre.md) — competing genre claims coexist as standpoint-indexed statements.

### Avoid when

- Avoid building a genre subclass tree or anointing one genre as the privileged winner of a dispute (Principles 5, 9), and avoid conflating genre with the work's kind ([`gmeow:CreativeWorkType`](gmeow-CreativeWorkType.md)).

### How to use

- Mint each genre as an individual of [`gmeow:Genre`](gmeow-Genre.md), record its lineage with [`gmeow:wasDerivedFrom`](../properties/gmeow-wasDerivedFrom.md), and attach it to works via [`gmeow:hasGenre`](../properties/gmeow-hasGenre.md); carry disputes on the statement layer rather than as a winner.

### Examples

- ex:bebop a [`gmeow:Genre`](gmeow-Genre.md); [`gmeow:wasDerivedFrom`](../properties/gmeow-wasDerivedFrom.md) ex:swing.
